entities.summary: Prince Nikolai Borisovich Yusupov was a Russian nobleman and art collector of the House of Yusupov, born into the aristocracy of 19th-century Russia. He was a prominent figure in St. Petersburg's high society, known for his extensive art collection and lavish parties. His family's fortune was built on the back of the Russian Empire's expansion, with his ancestors playing key roles in the conquest of Siberia and the establishment of the Amur Oblast. Yusupov's own contributions were significant, as he helped to establish the Imperial Russian Museum, which would later become the State Russian Museum. He was also a patron of the arts, supporting prominent artists such as Ivan Aivazovsky and Karl Briullov. However, his life was also marked by tragedy, including the infamous murder of Rasputin in 1916, which would go on to become a defining moment in Russian history. The event, which was orchestrated by Yusupov and his co-conspirators, was a turning point in the Russian Revolution and had far-reaching consequences for the country's future. As a result, Yusupov's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the grandeur of the Russian Empire and the darker aspects of its history.
